strengths: MU-Mis proposes an interesting unlearning objective based on class-specific input sensitivities. Its updates require only the pretrained model and forgetting data, which is practically useful when retained data are unavailable.
Full-class deletion results show promising utility preservation. On CIFAR-100, retained accuracy is 76.32% versus 76.36% before unlearning, while forgetting-class accuracy drops to zero.

The evaluation includes retraining, several relevant baselines, three deletion settings, and runtime comparisons. Table 6 provides useful evidence that combining the two loss terms substantially improves retained accuracy over suppressing target-class sensitivity alone.
weaknesses: The central derivation in Section 3.2 does not establish the claimed relationship between training contribution and input sensitivity. Differentiation with respect to training data omits dependencies through the loss gradient and training trajectory without justifying these omissions. Moreover, g g′ᵀ is not generally symmetric for multiclass outputs, so the asserted equality C_k = S_k does not generally hold. The accumulated cross-sample residual is also assumed negligible without a bound or direct measurement, and sensitivity to coordinate perturbations is not equivalent to deleting a sample.

Reducing Equation (1) is not shown to remove information or approach retraining. For example, adding the same input-dependent function to every logit preserves all softmax probabilities while generally changing the proposed squared-sensitivity difference. Thus, this objective can change without changing predictive evidence of membership. The sensitivity histograms and attention visualizations do not resolve this gap.

The privacy evaluation cannot convincingly distinguish unlearning from doing nothing. In Table 5, the pretrained model and MU-Mis have identical retained and forgotten accuracies; their MIA rates are 95% and 94%, respectively, while retraining also yields 94%. Matching this weakly discriminating metric does not establish deletion. Reporting only the fraction classified as members, without nonmember false-positive rates, calibrated attacks, or uncertainty, leaves the main privacy claim unsupported.

Experimental coverage is insufficient for the claimed consistent, significant superiority: all experiments use ResNet18, deletion targets cover few classes, and random deletion removes only 100 CIFAR-10 examples. There are no reported repeated-run statistics, deletion-size sweeps, or stopping-threshold ablations. Small gains such as 0.26 percentage points over SSD in Table 1 cannot establish significance. SalUn is cited but not compared.

Important reproduction details are missing, particularly actual stopping thresholds, their selection procedure, evaluation splits, and baseline tuning. Algorithm 1 initializes the current loss accumulator but never updates it, making the stated stopping statistic constant as written; its nested stopping loops are also unclear. These omissions matter because the objective has an unbounded negative term and depends on controlled stopping. Code is only promised, and absolute retraining timings supporting the claimed speedups are omitted.
